🔴 **Content edits erase Concept assessments** A content-only edit makes `syncChangedNodesToSupabase` rewrite its Concept, resetting an existing epistemic status to `unknown`. The database upsert defaults omitted Concept fields before replacing the row, so it also clears an existing description.
Learn more A Concept stores an epistemic status and description separately from a note's Content. [discourseNodeInstanceToLocalConcept](https://github.com/discoursegraphs/discourse-graph/blob/15fa6ae1094769bbbd55f88c95b8e0f7c8fb27e5/apps/obsidian/src/utils/conceptConversion.ts#L162-L197 "apps/obsidian/src/utils/conceptConversion.ts:162-197") does not supply either field. [upsert_concepts](https://github.com/discoursegraphs/discourse-graph/blob/15fa6ae1094769bbbd55f88c95b8e0f7c8fb27e5/packages/database/supabase/schemas/concept.sql#L480-L510 "packages/database/supabase/schemas/concept.sql:480-510") defaults the status to `unknown` and replaces both fields when updating an existing Concept. Previously a content-only edit sent only Content, so these fields were left untouched. The new content-only Concept write resets them even though the note did not change its Concept metadata. **Example:** A Concept has `epistemic_status = 'strong_evidence_for'` and `description = 'Reviewed'`. Editing only the note body syncs the full Content but changes those Concept fields to `unknown` and null. **Recommended fix:** Preserve existing Concept-only fields on content-only writes, either by changing the database upsert contract to distinguish omitted fields from explicit resets or by providing a dedicated Content update path. Keep the inline Content atomicity requirement in mind when choosing the approach.
